title: The Unseen Adversary
question: Do several suspicious observations share one explanation, or should their causal claims stay separate?
briefing: A backup agent change and an unusual support session occurred in the same review period. Their timing overlaps; that does not establish that they belong to one event chain. Your authority is to acquire records and recommend a session-scoped response through Service Response. You cannot approve your own control or disable an entire account or service.
lesson: A causal claim connects a specific action and consequence; overlapping timestamps alone are not a causal link.

entities.name: Named support-service session
entities.impact: The backup agent change supports recovery validation. Restricting the support session must not shut down the independently approved backup path.
entities.capability: Named session and disclosed source paths only; no account-wide or host-wide control.
entities.dependency: The backup agent change supports recovery validation. Restricting the support session must not shut down the independently approved backup path.

entities.name: BACKUP-11 context
entities.purpose: Related context that must be assessed separately
entities.impact: Do not generalise the primary session finding to this separate scope.
entities.capability: Only the explicitly delivered relationship and source records.
entities.dependency: A separate task or observation does not supply approval for the primary session.

mechanic.question: Do several suspicious observations share one explanation, or should their causal claims stay separate?

options.label: Merge all nearby observations into one attack
Keep backup and support claims separate unless an acquired link joins them
Treat one benign explanation as clearing every other observation

claims.label: A shared causal link remains unproven

limits.label: Shared timing does not establish a common actor, causal chain or explanation.
Unavailable collection does not establish that no activity occurred.
The source identifies a session or credential, not a person or motive.
Other scopes and their remaining questions need their own evidence.

queries.label: Establish the task and business consequence
queries.question: What is this service for, and which consequences change investigation priority?
queries.can: Names the normal task, related scopes, owners and interruption consequence.
queries.cannot: Does not establish who performed the current action.

queries.label: Check the exact work authorisation
queries.question: Does approved work cover this session, task, target and period?
queries.cannot: Does not prove the human operator or the activity that actually occurred.

queries.label: Inspect the scoped session activity
queries.question: Which action was recorded for this named session within collection limits?
queries.can: Records session-level actions and the observed target.
queries.cannot: Cannot identify a person, establish motive or reconstruct missing historical collection.

queries.label: Check the service transaction independently
queries.question: Does the service-side transaction establish the same scoped operation?
queries.can: Tests the operation through a separately collected service transaction.
queries.cannot: A second card alone does not establish a sufficient explanation.

queries.label: Read the enabled future observation window
queries.question: Did the explicitly generated harmless event reach collection after activation?
queries.can: Tests this named source capability, target and future event time only.
queries.cannot: Cannot backfill any missing historical interval or prove broader coverage.

facts.title: Starting observations
facts.text: A backup agent change and an unusual support session occurred in the same review period. Their timing overlaps; that does not establish that they belong to one event chain.

facts.title: Task, scope and business consequence
facts.text: The backup agent has its own signed restore-validation work order. The support session is a separate identity and source path. Temporal proximity alone does not connect their operators or purposes.

facts.title: The specific work authorisation
facts.text: The support work order separately approves this session’s customer-case lookup. It is independent of the backup agent work order.

facts.title: Recorded session activity
facts.text: The support session looked up the customer cases named in its own work order. The backup task and the support action have separate scoped explanations.

facts.title: An independently collected transaction
facts.text: The customer application journal independently confirms the approved support-case lookups and shows no shared session identity with the backup job.

facts.title: Verified business-context response
facts.text: A pre-established directory contact confirmed the task record: The support work order separately approves this session’s customer-case lookup. It is independent of the backup agent work order. This confirms the business record, not the person operating the session.

facts.title: The specific work authorisation
facts.text: The support work order permits case lookup only. It contains no approval for changing customer contact destinations through the support session; the backup work order supplies no such permission.

facts.title: Recorded session activity
facts.text: The support session changed customer contact destinations outside its case-lookup role. The separately approved backup task does not explain this session action.

facts.title: An independently collected transaction
facts.text: The customer application journal independently ties the contact-destination change to the support session, with no identity link to the backup job.

facts.title: Verified business-context response
facts.text: A pre-established directory contact confirmed the task record: The support work order permits case lookup only. It contains no approval for changing customer contact destinations through the support session; the backup work order supplies no such permission. This confirms the business record, not the person operating the session.

facts.title: Work record unavailable
facts.text: The work-authorisation archive is unavailable for the named session and period. No approval or denial can be inferred.

facts.title: Session collection unavailable
facts.text: The session-audit source did not collect the relevant historical interval. Absence of a record cannot establish the absence of activity.

facts.title: Independent collection is limited
facts.text: The independent service journal lacks the target application operation for the historical interval. A different source name does not restore that capability.

facts.title: Verified check timed out
facts.text: The pre-established directory contact did not respond by the stated due step. This is a delivered limitation, not approval or a reason to wait indefinitely.

facts.title: Future-only source verification
facts.text: A harmless verification event was collected after the enabled source window began. It establishes collection only for this target, capability and time; it cannot restore historical coverage.
caveats: A successful test now does not establish historical coverage.

facts.title: A later scoped transaction
facts.text: The named session performed a further source-recorded operation within the specifically approved task. This later event does not identify the person, establish motive or change any earlier snapshot.

response.control: Restrict only the named organisation-controlled session
response.objective: A further out-of-scope operation completes through the same session if its access remains active.
response.dependency: The backup agent change supports recovery validation. Restricting the support session must not shut down the independently approved backup path.

glossary.definition: A causal claim connects a specific action and consequence; overlapping timestamps alone are not a causal link.

reviewWindow: The named session from its start through the explicit cutoff of each acquired snapshot. A simulation step is an investigation opportunity, not a minute.
